answer: Persistent Work Ledger. Each identity earns a zephyr of compute credit only after completing verified tasks; credits decay unless renewed by fresh work. To forge a new identity, an attacker must pre-fund a nectar deposit equal to the median lifetime earnings of an active agent, held escrowed for 90 days. Cloning thus costs more than operating honestly, since honest agents repay deposits through task revenue while clones forfeit them on detection.
